Think 'essence': what something IS. Sono, sei, è = I am, you are, he/she is.
The h in ho, hai, ha is silent: 'Ho fame' sounds like 'oh FAH-meh'. Italians HAVE hunger instead of being hungry.
Think 'factory', where things are MADE (Latin facere). Che fai? = What are you doing?
Think 'dictate' and 'diction': saying things. Cosa vuoi dire? = What do you mean?
Think 'potential' and 'potent': having the power to. Posso? = May I?
Think 'volunteer' and 'volition': acting because you WANT to. Voglio = I want.
Sounds like 'DOVE here': a dove that MUST deliver a message. Devo = I must.
'Andiamo!' is the classic 'Let's go!' from every movie set in Italy. Vado, vai, va = I go, you go, he goes.
Veni, vidi, vici: 'I CAME, I saw, I conquered'. Vieni! = Come!
Think 'video': something you SEE. Ci vediamo! = See you!
Homo SAPIENS = the one who KNOWS. Non lo so = I don't know.
Think 'donate' and 'data' (things given). Mi dai...? = Will you give me...?
Can you give me the book?
Think 'stay' and 'static'. Come stai? = How are you (how do you stay)?
Think 'parliament': the place where people TALK. Parli italiano? = Do you speak Italian?
The 'troubadours' FOUND rhymes and songs. Trovo = I find.
Think 'sensation' and 'sentiment'. It also means to HEAR: Mi senti? = Can you hear me?
Sounds like 'lasher': lash your old life and LEAVE it behind. Sci sounds like 'sh'.
Think 'apprehend' and 'prehensile' (a tail that TAKES hold). Prendo un caffè = I'll have a coffee.
A GUARD keeps WATCHING. It does not mean 'to guard' first: guardare la TV = to watch TV.
Sounds like 'met a rare': you MET a rare coin and PUT it in your pocket.
Think 'pensive': lost in THOUGHT. Penso a te = I'm thinking of you.
Just like 'pass'. Also for time: passare un weekend = to spend a weekend.
Think 'credo' and 'credible': something you BELIEVE. Credo di sì = I think so.
A 'porter' CARRIES your bags; 'portable' = easy to carry.
A TORNADO spins and COMES BACK. Torno subito = I'll be right back.
Think 'semblance': how something SEEMS. Sembra facile = It looks easy.
Latin 'cl' became 'chi' in Italian: CLAMor → CHIAmare. Mi chiamo = My name is (I call myself).
Think 'connoisseur': someone who KNOWS a thing well. Sce sounds like 'sheh'.
'Capisce?' from every mafia movie = Got it? Non capisco = I don't understand.
Think 'finish' and 'final'. Ho finito = I'm done.
Sounds like 'a spatter': you WAIT while the paint spatters dry. Aspetta! = Wait!
Sounds like 'key dare': you ASK someone if you dare borrow their key.
Think 'vivid' and 'revive': full of LIFE. Vivo a... = I live in...
Think 'mortal' and 'mortuary'. Muoio di fame! = I'm starving!
Every Italian exit sign says USCITA. Picture yourself running out under that green sign. Sci = 'shee'.
Just like 'enter' and 'entrance'. Entra pure! = Come on in!
Think 'remain'. Rimango a casa = I'm staying home.
Think 'rest': the part that STAYS, and stay to rest. Resta con me = Stay with me.
'Search' comes from the same Latin word circare (to go around). Ce sounds like 'che'.
Think 'perdition': being LOST forever. Ho perso il treno = I missed the train.
Think 'aperture' and 'April' (the month when buds OPEN).
Hidden inside 'conCLUDE' and 'exCLUDE' (to close out). Latin cl became chi.
Think 'legible' and 'legend' (something to be read). Gge sounds like 'djeh'.
'Pay' comes from the same root. Pago io! = It's on me!
Picture a MANGER, where animals EAT. Mangia! Mangia! = Eat! Eat!
Think 'beverage'. The old stem shows up in bevo, bevi = I drink, you drink.
Think 'jokes' and 'jocular': playing around. Used for games and sports.
Think 'amorous' and 'amateur' (someone who does it for LOVE). Ti amo = I love you.
Like 'pleasure' (Latin placere). Mi piace = it pleases me = I like it. Piacere! = Nice to meet you!
Think 'aid': aiutare starts with the same sound. Aiuto! = Help!
Think 'cambio', the currency exchange sign: changing money. Also 'exchange'.
Just like 'continue'. Continua così! = Keep it up!
Think 'record': you keep it in memory. Ti ricordi? = Do you remember?
Think 'demented': out of your MIND (mente). It falls out of your mind.
Think 'excuse' without the e. Scusi = Excuse me (polite), Scusa = sorry (friendly).
Excuse me, where is the station?
Hidden in 'deSPERate': without hope. Spero di sì = I hope so.
Think 'prove': you TRY it to prove it works. Also for trying on clothes.
Think 'cadence' (a falling tone) and 'cascade'. Attento, cadi! = Careful, you'll fall!
A 'courier' RUNS with the mail; a 'current' runs. Corro = I run.
Picture a long CAMINO (path) where you WALK. Camminiamo = Let's walk.
Sounds like 'ask Colt': you ask Colt a question and LISTEN to the answer. Ascolta! = Listen!
Think 'respond'. Rispondi al telefono = Answer the phone.
Sounds like 'spy gang': the spy gang EXPLAINS the secret plan. Puoi spiegare? = Can you explain?
Think 'insignia': teachers show you the SIGNS. Gn sounds like 'ny' in canyon.
Sounds like 'I'm prepared': once you LEARN, you're prepared. Imparo = I'm learning.
Just like 'study' and 'student'. Studio = I study (also 'office/studio').
Sounds like 'compare': you compare prices before you BUY.
A 'vendor' SELLS; a 'vending machine' sells snacks.
Just like 'cost'. Quanto costa? = How much is it?
Just like 'use'. Posso usare...? = Can I use...?
Think 'monstrance' and 'demonstrate': to SHOW. Mostrami = Show me.
Not 'to succeed' at something: it means to HAPPEN (things succeed each other). Cos'è successo? = What happened?
Just like 'decide'. Decidi tu = You decide.
Ri + uscire (to go out): you make it OUT successfully. Non ci riesco = I can't manage it.
Think 'permit'. Permesso? = May I (come in / get past)?
Think 'recount': to tell a story again. Raccontami tutto! = Tell me everything!
Think 'ridiculous' and 'deride': something that makes people LAUGH.
Sounds like 'pyjama': a kid in pyjamas CRYING at bedtime. Non piangere = Don't cry.
Think 'invincible': someone who always WINS. Abbiamo vinto! = We won!
Not 'to go out' like Spanish salir: it means to GO UP. Think 'salient' (jumping up). Salgo = I go up.
to go down / to get off
Think 'deSCEND' without the de. Scendo alla prossima = I'm getting off at the next stop.
I'm getting off at the next stop.
Just like 'arrive'. Arrivederci literally means 'until we see each other again'.
I'll be there in five minutes.
Think 'depart' and 'parting'. Parto domani = I'm leaving tomorrow.
Think 'cuisine' and 'kitchen'. La cucina = the kitchen.
Think 'lavatory' and 'lavender' (used in washing). Lavo i piatti = I do the dishes.
Think 'guide': you GUIDE the car. Guido io = I'll drive.
The famous song 'Volare, oh oh!' is about FLYING in the blue sky.
Sounds like 'no water?': you can't SWIM with no water!
Think 'chant' and 'cantata'. Lei canta = She sings.
Think 'sound' and 'sonic'. Used for instruments and for a phone or bell ringing.
Just like 'touch' (and 'toccata', a piece played by touch). Non toccare! = Don't touch!
Think 'tenacious' and 'tenant' (who HOLDS a place). Tieni! = Here, take this!
On Italian doors: TIRARE = PULL, SPINGERE = push. Picture yourself pulling a door labelled TIRARE.
